@clayjohn just wanted to point out this check, this safeguards against the main issue that causes projection matrices to fail in the rendering engine and result in improper lighting. It's also why the transform offset is added instead of pre-multiplied with the projection matrix.

Yes there are possibly scenarios where people still submit some crazy projection matrix that doesn't fail this check, but unless we have an actual use case that shows a projection matrix that actually falsely passes this check... :shrug:

Our original conclusion many moons ago that we couldn't unproject matrices properly actually turned out to be false. At the time we had a number of faults in the rendering code where `m[2][0]` and `m[2][1]` were incorrectly applied, most likely due to all the y-flip stuff. It never stood out because for symmetrical matrices these are always zero and had no impact on the rendered result.

But since we introduced the "frustum" mode to `Camera3D`, we've been fixing all those because they started standing out like a sore thumb. The last of which [was an issue in GI](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117619) that we merged a few weeks ago.

Also we did some funky y-reflip nonsense for the frustum mode that hid the core problem, [I cleaned that up as well](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116752).

I can probably do more cleanup around some of the `USE_MULTIVIEW` implementation and do our quick unproject now, but since those ifdefs are still needed for reason unrelated to this PR I had a "if it ain't broke, don't try to fix it" mentality. Worth a follow up PR but would just be noise in this PR.
